title: Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day
content_md: Amazon says autonomous AI agents run by a China-linked threat actor found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability in MONAI Label, an open source tool designed for AI-assisted annotation of medical images. The tech giant’s threat intelligence team detected the activity in September, after coming across an exposed instance of Cairn , an open source AI penetration testing framework. The instance had no authentication, so anyone could see the operator’s prompts and the agents’ output. The records showed a roughly 48-hour campaign against IP addresses belonging to universities in East Asia outside mainland China. The operator gave the agents a list of targets and told them to obtain shell access. After identifying the software on one target and mapping its API, the agents discovered a path traversal bug in a file upload function. “In about 11 minutes, the agents went from mapping the application’s API to arbitrarily writing files on the server,” Amazon said . In a later session, the agents used the flaw to plant a Python reverse shell in a file Python runs every time the interpreter starts, ultimately achieving a root shell. “Amazon Threat Intelligence assesses with high confidence that it was a zero-day based on the absence of any corresponding fix, issue, advisory, or prior mention in vulnerability databases for the affected open-source project,” the company said.
